description:
The one pre-existing archive directory whose name came from an issue title is renamed to its bare short id, and its container marker still resolves the renamed directory.

## Background

Exactly one archive directory carries a title-derived name, truncated mid-word. Its owning issue's type has no configured membership namespace, so under the naming rule without a title fallback its name becomes the bare short id — the same shape a second, older archive directory already uses and that the resolver already adopts.

The container marker holds the owning container's full identifier and nothing else; it encodes no directory name. That independence is what makes the rename safe: after the move, the marker still matches, the resolver re-adopts the directory by marker, and a rerun of the plan converges instead of creating a second destination.

The hand-made semantic subdirectories elsewhere in the archive are legacy and are not migrated. They carry no marker and are not identifier-shaped, so they are outside this work.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The title-slugged archive directory is renamed to its bare short id with its contents intact.
- [hard] REQ-02: The container marker file is unchanged and still names the owning container's full identifier.
- [hard] REQ-03: A preview for that container resolves the renamed directory as its destination and plans no second destination.
- [hard] REQ-04: The hand-made semantic subdirectories under the archive root are left as they are.
- [hard] REQ-05: Whole-repository validation passes after the rename.
title: Rename the title-slugged archive directory to its bare short id
